notes: DRAFT for scholarly review. English only; Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quranic text in the repo (Tanzil Uthmani) only; no hadith, no tafsir, no Gospel or other scripture, no sira in this phase. Hadith to add later: reports on the descent of Isa, on the Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus), and on the table (al-ma'idah). Names and details found only in later tradition are kept in unknowns_md and uncertainties_en. Quotation marks surround only speech recorded in the cited ayat (English renderings are drafts for translator and scholar review). This draft takes no position on questions where classical interpreters differ (the meaning of 'mutawaffika' in 3:55, the manner of the raising, the pronoun in 4:159); it states the words and marks the question. Nothing here is reviewed or published.

chapters.title_en: The wife of Imran and Maryam

claims.statement_en: The wife of Imran said “My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated; so accept it from me; You are the Hearing, the Knowing.”

When she gave birth she said “My Lord, I have given birth to a female”, and Allah knew best what she had given birth to, “and the male is not like the female; I have named her Maryam, and I seek refuge for her and her offspring in You from Shaytan, the accursed.”
Her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and made her grow in a good growth, and made Zakariyya her guardian.

Whenever Zakariyya entered upon her in the mihrab he found provision with her; he said “Maryam, from where is this for you?” and she said “It is from Allah; Allah provides for whom He wills without account.”

Allah tells the listener that this is of the news of the unseen which He reveals, and that the listener was not with those who cast their pens to decide which of them would take charge of Maryam, nor with them when they disputed.

chapters.summary_md: The wife of Imran vowed the child in her womb [c1]. She gave birth to a girl and named her Maryam [c2]. Allah accepted Maryam, and Zakariyya became her guardian [c3]; he found provision with her [c4]. Allah says this is news of the unseen [c5].
chapters.body_md: The wife of Imran said she had vowed to her Lord what was in her womb, dedicated, and asked Him to accept it [c1]. When she gave birth she said she had delivered a female, that the male is not like the female, that she had named her Maryam, and that she sought refuge for her and her offspring with Allah from Shaytan, the accursed [c2]. Her Lord accepted her with good acceptance, made her grow in a good growth, and made Zakariyya her guardian [c3]. Whenever he came upon her in the mihrab he found provision with her, and she told him it was from Allah, who provides for whom He wills without account [c4]. Allah adds that this is news of the unseen, and that the listener was not with those who cast their pens over who would take charge of Maryam [c5].
chapters.deep_md: Four statements are made about Maryam in a single sequence: her mother's vow and prayer [c1][c2], Allah's acceptance [c3], Zakariyya's finding of provision [c4], and the casting of pens over her care [c5]. The text does not say that these are consecutive in time, and the ayat give no number of years between them. Maryam's own words in this chapter are a single sentence [c4]. The words ‘dedicated’ (muharraran) and ‘acceptance’ are the same pair that frame the passage [c1][c3].
chapters.kids_md: The wife of Imran asked Allah to accept the child she carried. When her baby was born, she named her Maryam and asked Allah to protect her [c1][c2]. Allah accepted Maryam, and Zakariyya took care of her [c3]. When he found food with her, she told him it was from Allah [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the chapter links a mother's prayer [c2], a guardian's care [c3] and a young woman's answer that her provision is from Allah [c4]. It may prompt reflection on dedication and trust.
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: the name of Imran's wife, the dates, how the casting of pens was done, what kind of provision Zakariyya found, and what the mihrab was (the ayat use the word without describing a place). Whether this Imran is the same as the father of Musa and Harun in tradition is not stated; 66:12 calls Maryam 'daughter of Imran'. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the personal name of Maryam's mother, and the place of her upbringing.

claims.statement_en: The angels said “Maryam, Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you over the women of the worlds”, and “Maryam, be devout to your Lord, and prostrate and bow with those who bow.”
The angels said “Maryam, Allah gives you glad tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near.”
He will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity, and is of the righteous.
She said “My Lord, how can I have a child when no human has touched me?” and was told “Thus Allah creates what He wills; when He decrees a matter He only says to it ‘Be’, and it is.”
In Surah Maryam, she withdrew from her family to an eastern place and took a screen from them; Allah sent to her “Our Spirit”.
She said “I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are mindful of Him.” He said “I am only a messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure boy.”

She said “How can I have a boy when no human has touched me and I have not been unchaste?” He said “So it is. Your Lord says: It is easy for Me; and so that We make him a sign for the people and a mercy from Us; and it is a matter decreed.”

chapters.summary_md: The angels told Maryam that Allah had chosen and purified her [c1]. They gave her glad tidings of a word from Him whose name is the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam [c2], who would speak in the cradle and in maturity [c3]. She asked how she could have a child [c4][c7], and was told it is easy for Allah [c7]. Surah Maryam tells it with Allah's Spirit sent to her [c5][c6].
chapters.body_md:
The angels said to Maryam that Allah had chosen her, purified her and chosen her over the women of the worlds, and told her to be devout, to prostrate and to bow with those who bow [c1]. They gave her glad tidings of a word from Allah whose name is the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near [c2]. He would speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity and be of the righteous [c3]. She asked how she could have a child when no human had touched her, and was told that Allah creates what He wills, and when He decrees a matter He says to it ‘Be’ and it is [c4].

Surah Maryam tells that she withdrew from her family to an eastern place and took a screen from them, and Allah sent to her Our Spirit [c5]. She said she sought refuge in the Most Merciful if the one who came was mindful of Him; he said he was only a messenger of her Lord, to give her a pure boy [c6]. She asked how she could have a boy when no human had touched her and she had not been unchaste, and he said it was so, that it was easy for her Lord, that He would make him a sign for the people and a mercy from Him, and that it was a matter decreed [c7].
chapters.deep_md: Two surahs tell the announcement with a different speaker: ‘the angels’ in Al Imran [c1][c2] and ‘Our Spirit’, who calls himself a messenger of her Lord, in Maryam [c5][c6]. The question of the mother is the same in both and is answered in similar terms [c4][c7]. The name and titles are given in Al Imran: ‘a word from Him’, ‘the Messiah’, ‘Isa son of Maryam’ [c2]. The phrase ‘a sign for the people and a mercy from Us’ is given in Maryam [c7]. The cradle speech is announced here [c3] and told in a later chapter.
chapters.kids_md: Angels told Maryam that Allah had chosen her [c1]. They gave her good news of a baby called Isa [c2]. Maryam asked how she could have a baby, and she was told that Allah creates whatever He wants [c4]. Allah said it is easy for Him [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the ayat show a young woman asking a sincere question and being answered directly [c4][c7]; they begin with being told to be devout [c1].
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: the place in the east, the date, the name of the one who came (the ayat say 'Our Spirit' and 'a messenger of your Lord'; Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name Jibril, which hadith literature and tafsir give; hadith to add later), and how the 'screen' was set. The meaning of 'a word from Him' (kalimatun minhu) is read in more than one way by interpreters; this draft gives the words only. The ayat describe the form in which the messenger appeared only as stated in 19:17, which is not described here.

claims.statement_en: She conceived him and withdrew with him to a remote place.
The pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree; she said “If only I had died before this and had been something forgotten and lost.”
She was called from beneath her: “Do not grieve; your Lord has placed beneath you a sariyy.”

She was told “Shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you fresh ripe dates. So eat and drink and be comforted. If you see any human, say ‘I have vowed a fast to the Most Merciful, so I will not speak today to any human’.”
Allah says that He breathed into the one who guarded her chastity of His spirit, and made her and her son a sign for the worlds.
Allah says that He made the son of Maryam and his mother a sign, and gave them refuge on a high ground, a place of rest and of flowing water.
Maryam, daughter of Imran, guarded her chastity, and Allah breathed into it of His spirit; she believed in the words of her Lord and His books, and was of the devout.

chapters.summary_md: Maryam conceived and withdrew to a remote place [c1]. In labour she came to the trunk of a palm tree and said she wished she had died before this [c2]. She was called not to grieve, told of a sariyy beneath her [c3], and told to shake the palm tree, eat and drink, and say she had vowed a fast [c4]. Other surahs call her and her son a sign [c5][c6][c7].
chapters.body_md:
Maryam conceived him and withdrew with him to a remote place [c1]. The pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree, and she said she wished she had died before this and been something forgotten and lost [c2]. She was called from beneath her not to grieve, because her Lord had placed beneath her a sariyy [c3]. She was told to shake the trunk of the palm tree toward her so that fresh ripe dates would fall, to eat and drink and be comforted, and if she saw any human, to say that she had vowed a fast to the Most Merciful and would not speak that day to any human [c4].

Other surahs speak of the same woman. Al-Anbiya says Allah breathed into her of His spirit and made her and her son a sign for the worlds [c5]. Al-Mu'minun says that Allah made the son of Maryam and his mother a sign and gave them refuge on a high ground with rest and flowing water [c6]. At-Tahrim names Maryam, daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity and was breathed into of Allah's spirit; she believed in the words of her Lord and His books and was of the devout [c7].
chapters.deep_md: Three further surahs summarise the same event in one sentence each [c5][c6][c7] and all use the word ‘sign’ or an equivalent for her and her son, except At-Tahrim, which gives her belief and devotion [c7]. In Surah Maryam, the account moves from her grief [c2] to a series of instructions [c3][c4]; the ayat do not say who called her from beneath her, and they do not say what the word sariyy refers to (a stream or a noble one are both discussed by interpreters). The ‘high ground’ of Al-Mu'minun [c6] is not stated to be the place of 19:22.
chapters.kids_md: Maryam went to a quiet place, and when the baby was about to be born she came to a palm tree [c1][c2]. She was told not to be sad, and to shake the palm tree so that dates would fall for her to eat [c3][c4]. Allah says that she and her son are a sign for everyone [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the account records a woman in distress being given food and drink and told not to grieve [c3][c4]. The surahs also record that she believed in the words of her Lord and was devout [c7].
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: the place, the date, who called to her from beneath her (19:24), what the word sariyy means here, what the “remote place” and the “high ground” refer to, and the number of days or months. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the names of the places given in tradition for the birth. The details of her fast of silence beyond the sentence in 19:26 are not given.

claims.statement_en: She came to her people carrying him; they said “Maryam, you have done a monstrous thing. Sister of Harun, your father was not a man of evil and your mother was not unchaste.”
She pointed to him; they said “How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?”
He said “I am the servant of Allah; He has given me the Book and made me a prophet.”
He said “He has made me blessed wherever I am, and enjoined on me prayer and zakat as long as I live, and dutiful to my mother, and has not made me a tyrant, wretched.”
He said “Peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised alive.”
Allah says “That is Isa, son of Maryam — the word of truth about which they dispute.”
Allah says it is not for Him to take a son — glory be to Him; when He decrees a matter He only says to it ‘Be’, and it is.
The ayat state: “Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is a straight path.” (The ayah does not mark the speaker.)
In Surah Al Imran, the angels told Maryam in advance that he would speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity.

chapters.summary_md: Maryam came to her people with the child and they reproached her [c1]. She pointed to him [c2], and he said he was the servant of Allah who had given him the Book and made him a prophet [c3]. He spoke of prayer, zakat and dutifulness to his mother [c4] and of peace upon him on three days [c5]. Allah says this is the word of truth about which they dispute [c6].
chapters.body_md:
She came to her people carrying him, and they said she had done a monstrous thing and reminded her that her father was not a man of evil and her mother was not unchaste, addressing her as ‘sister of Harun’ [c1]. She pointed to him, and they asked how they could speak to one in the cradle, a child [c2]. He said “I am the servant of Allah; He has given me the Book and made me a prophet” [c3]. He said Allah had made him blessed wherever he was, had enjoined on him prayer and zakat as long as he lived, made him dutiful to his mother and had not made him a tyrant, wretched [c4]. He said “Peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised alive” [c5].

Allah says this is Isa, son of Maryam, the word of truth about which they dispute [c6], and that it is not for Allah to take a son; when He decrees a matter He only says to it ‘Be’ and it is [c7]. The next ayah states that Allah is the Lord of both and calls to worship Him, as a straight path [c8]. Al Imran had already told Maryam that he would speak in the cradle and in maturity [c9].
chapters.deep_md: The cradle speech in Surah Maryam is a short list of statements about himself, in the first person: his servanthood and prophethood [c3], his blessing and obligations [c4], and peace on the three days [c5]. The text immediately follows with Allah's own words on the subject of dispute [c6][c7]. The speaker of 19:36 [c8] is not marked in the ayah; interpreters read it as Isa's words or as Allah's, and this draft makes no choice. The statement in Al Imran that he would speak ‘in the cradle and in maturity’ [c9] announces the same event.
chapters.kids_md: When Maryam brought her baby to her people, they were upset. She pointed to the baby. The baby said, “I am the servant of Allah; He has given me the Book and made me a prophet” [c1][c2][c3]. He also said that Allah had told him to pray and to be good to his mother [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the first words recorded of Isa are about being a servant of Allah [c3]. The chapter may be read as a reminder that his own statement of his role comes first and precedes any claim made about him by others.
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: the day or place of the cradle speech, who the people were, the exact sense of ‘sister of Harun’ in 19:28 (interpreters discuss whether it refers to a brother named Harun, a descent from Harun the brother of Musa, or a figurative address; Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any of those identifications; hadith to add later), the speaker of 19:36, and what is meant by ‘the Book’ he was given at that time. The ayat do not say whether the ‘maturity’ speech of 3:46 is recorded in the Quran beyond the later chapters of this draft.

claims.statement_en: Allah will teach him the Book, the wisdom, the Torah and the Injil.
He will be a messenger to the Children of Israel, who says “I have come to you with a sign from your Lord.”

He said “I create for you from clay the likeness of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by Allah's permission; I heal the blind from birth and the leper, and I bring the dead to life by Allah's permission; and I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. In that is a sign for you, if you are believers.”
He said “I confirm what is before me of the Torah and I make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you; I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so be mindful of Allah and obey me.”
He said “Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is a straight path.”

In Surah Al-Ma'idah, Allah recalls to Isa His favour upon him and his mother: He strengthened him with the Holy Spirit so that he spoke to people in the cradle and in maturity, taught him the Book, the wisdom, the Torah and the Injil, he created from clay the likeness of a bird by Allah's permission and breathed into it and it became a bird by His permission, healed the blind from birth and the leper by His permission, and brought the dead out by His permission.
Allah says He restrained the Children of Israel from him when he came to them with clear proofs, and those of them who disbelieved said “This is nothing but clear magic.”

In Surah Az-Zukhruf, when Isa came with clear proofs he said “I have come to you with wisdom, and to make clear to you some of what you differ about; so be mindful of Allah and obey me. Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is a straight path.”

chapters.summary_md: Isa was taught the Book, the wisdom, the Torah and the Injil [c1], and sent as a messenger to the Children of Israel [c2]. He said he made a bird-likeness from clay, healed the blind and the leper and brought the dead to life, all by Allah's permission [c3][c6]. He confirmed the Torah [c4] and told them to worship Allah, his Lord and theirs [c5][c8].
chapters.body_md:
Allah will teach him the Book, the wisdom, the Torah and the Injil [c1]. He will be a messenger to the Children of Israel, and say that he has come with a sign from their Lord [c2]. He said that he creates for them from clay the likeness of a bird, breathes into it and it becomes a bird by Allah's permission, heals the blind from birth and the leper, brings the dead to life by Allah's permission, and informs them of what they eat and store in their houses [c3]. He said he confirms what was before him of the Torah and makes lawful for them some of what was forbidden, and told them to be mindful of Allah and obey him [c4]. He said Allah is his Lord and theirs and told them to worship Him [c5].

In Al-Ma'idah, Allah recalls His favour on Isa and his mother: strengthening him with the Holy Spirit, teaching him, and the signs, each by His permission [c6]. He restrained the Children of Israel from him when he came with clear proofs, and those who disbelieved said it was clear magic [c7]. In Az-Zukhruf, Isa says he has come with wisdom and to make clear some of what they differ about, and again that Allah is his Lord and theirs [c8].
chapters.deep_md: The signs are listed twice with near-identical wording: as Isa's words to his people in Al Imran [c3] and as Allah's recollection in Al-Ma'idah [c6]. In both, each sign is qualified ‘by Allah's permission’ [c3][c6]. The statement ‘I confirm what is before me of the Torah’ [c4] appears with the lawful and the forbidden [c4]. The call to worship Allah, ‘my Lord and your Lord’, closes his speech in two surahs [c5][c8]. The people's response is recorded as ‘clear magic’ [c7].
chapters.kids_md: Allah taught Isa the Book and the wisdom [c1]. Isa was sent to the Children of Israel with signs from Allah [c2]. By Allah's permission he made a bird shape out of clay and it became a bird, and he healed people [c3]. He always told his people to worship Allah, his Lord and their Lord [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: every sign in the ayat is attributed ‘by Allah's permission’ [c3][c6], and the message that follows is to worship Allah [c5][c8]. A reader may reflect on how the ayat tie the signs to a call and not to the person.
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: where and when each sign took place, who was healed, who was brought back to life, how many signs there were, and what the Injil contained beyond the statement of 5:46. Hadith to add later: reports on the signs. The Injil and the Torah mentioned here are named as books given or confirmed; the text of any existing scripture of those names is outside this phase.

claims.statement_en: Allah sent Isa son of Maryam in the footsteps of the earlier prophets, confirming the Torah before him, and gave him the Injil, in which is guidance and light, confirming the Torah before it, and guidance and admonition for the mindful.

Allah sent Isa son of Maryam following in the footsteps of other messengers, gave him the Injil, and placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy; as for monasticism (rahbaniyyah), they invented it, and Allah did not prescribe it for them except seeking Allah's pleasure, but they did not observe it as it should have been observed.
Allah says He gave Isa son of Maryam the clear proofs and strengthened him with the Holy Spirit.
Isa son of Maryam said “Children of Israel, I am the messenger of Allah to you, confirming what is before me of the Torah and giving glad tidings of a messenger to come after me whose name is Ahmad.”
When that messenger came to them with clear proofs, they said “This is clear magic.”

chapters.summary_md: Allah sent Isa after the earlier prophets, confirming the Torah and giving him the Injil [c1][c2]. He gave him clear proofs and strengthened him with the Holy Spirit [c3]. Isa told the Children of Israel he was confirming the Torah and giving glad tidings of a messenger named Ahmad [c4].
chapters.body_md:
Allah sent Isa son of Maryam in the footsteps of earlier prophets, confirming the Torah before him, and gave him the Injil, in which is guidance and light and admonition for the mindful [c1]. Surah Al-Hadid adds that Allah put compassion and mercy in the hearts of those who followed him, and that monasticism was something they invented, which Allah did not prescribe except to seek His pleasure, though they did not observe it as it should have been observed [c2]. Surah Al-Baqarah says twice that Isa son of Maryam was given the clear proofs and strengthened with the Holy Spirit [c3].

Surah As-Saff records Isa's words to the Children of Israel: that he is the messenger of Allah, confirming the Torah, and giving glad tidings of a messenger after him whose name is Ahmad [c4]. The ayah continues that when that messenger came with clear proofs, they said “This is clear magic” [c5].
chapters.deep_md: Five ayat in four surahs place Isa among a line of messengers [c1][c2][c3]. They agree on his confirmation of the Torah [c1][c4] and on the Injil [c1][c2]. Only As-Saff 61:6 gives the glad tidings of a messenger named Ahmad [c4]; the ayah's last clause is about those to whom the messenger came [c5]. The ayah does not say, in these words, who is meant by ‘they’ in the last clause (the earlier audience or the later), and interpreters have read it in different ways.
chapters.kids_md: Isa came after other prophets and gave the same message. He had the Injil, with guidance and light [c1]. He told his people that a messenger named Ahmad would come after him [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the ayat set Isa within a series of messengers, each confirming the earlier [c1][c4]. They also record a limit in the response of some of his followers [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: the detail of what monasticism refers to in 57:27, the contents of the Injil, and who the Holy Spirit is (Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Jibril; hadith to add later). The identification of the messenger ‘whose name is Ahmad’ with Muhammad is treated in the Muhammad draft from this same ayah; 61:6 here states only the name and the glad tidings.

claims.statement_en: When Isa sensed disbelief from them, he said “Who will be my helpers to Allah?” The disciples (al-hawariyyun) said “We are the helpers of Allah; we believe in Allah, and bear witness that we are Muslims.”
They said “Our Lord, we believe in what You have sent down and we have followed the messenger, so write us with the witnesses.”
Allah says He inspired the disciples “Believe in Me and in My messenger”, and they said “We believe, and bear witness that we are Muslims.”
The disciples said “Isa son of Maryam, is your Lord able to send down to us a table from the heaven?” He said “Be mindful of Allah, if you are believers.”
They said “We wish to eat from it, that our hearts may be at rest, that we may know that you have told us the truth, and that we may be among its witnesses.”

Isa son of Maryam said “O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table from the heaven, to be a festival for the first of us and the last of us, and a sign from You; and provide for us, for You are the best of providers.”
Allah said “I will send it down to you; but whoever among you disbelieves afterward, I will punish him with a punishment with which I have not punished anyone among the worlds.”

In Surah As-Saff, believers are told to be helpers of Allah, as Isa son of Maryam said to the disciples “Who are my helpers to Allah?” and the disciples said “We are the helpers of Allah”; a group of the Children of Israel believed and a group disbelieved; Allah supported those who believed against their enemy and they became dominant.

chapters.summary_md: When Isa sensed disbelief he asked for helpers to Allah [c1]. The disciples said they were helpers of Allah and believers, and asked to be written with the witnesses [c1][c2]. Surah Al-Ma'idah records their request for a table from the heaven [c4][c5], Isa's prayer [c6] and Allah's answer [c7]. As-Saff calls believers to be helpers as the disciples were [c8].
chapters.body_md:
When Isa sensed disbelief from them, he asked “Who will be my helpers to Allah?” The disciples said they were helpers of Allah and bore witness that they were Muslims [c1], and asked to be written with the witnesses [c2]. Al-Ma'idah says Allah inspired the disciples to believe in Him and His messenger and they said they believed [c3]. They then asked whether his Lord was able to send down a table from the heaven; he told them to be mindful of Allah [c4]. They said they wished to eat from it, to have their hearts at rest, to know he had told them the truth and to be witnesses [c5]. Isa prayed for the table, to be a festival for the first and the last and a sign, and for provision [c6]. Allah said He would send it down, with a warning of a punishment unlike any other for whoever disbelieved afterward [c7].

As-Saff calls on the believers to be helpers of Allah, as the disciples were, and says a group of the Children of Israel believed and a group disbelieved, and Allah supported those who believed and they became dominant [c8].
chapters.deep_md: The disciples' words are given in three surahs with two themes: helping Allah [c1][c8] and bearing witness that they are Muslims [c1][c3]. The table [c4]-[c7] appears only in Al-Ma'idah. The ayat 5:112-115 record a request, a conditional prayer and a warning, and do not narrate the table itself being sent down or eaten; the ayat that follow are not part of this draft. The word al-hawariyyun is left transliterated.
chapters.kids_md: Isa asked, “Who will be my helpers to Allah?” and the disciples said, “We are the helpers of Allah” [c1]. They asked Isa for a table of food from the sky, so that their hearts would be at rest. Isa asked Allah, and Allah said He would send it [c4][c5][c6][c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the disciples first state their faith [c1] and then ask for reassurance [c5]; the ayat record both. The ayat also record the warning attached to the answer [c7].
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: how many disciples there were, their names, where they lived, what the table held or whether it was sent down (the ayat of 5:115 record the promise), and who the 'group' of 61:14 were. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the names and number of the disciples and the content of the table. Hadith to add later: reports on the table.

chapters.title_en: The matter of the cross and the raising

claims.statement_en: They plotted and Allah plotted, and Allah is the best of plotters.

Allah said “Isa, I am mutawaffika and the One raising you to Myself, and the One purifying you from those who disbelieve, and make those who follow you above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection; then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you differed.” (The word mutawaffika is left untranslated; interpreters differ on its sense.)

Allah mentions their saying “We killed the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, the messenger of Allah” and says they did not kill him and did not crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them (shubbiha lahum).
Those who differ about it are in doubt about it; they have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption; and they did not kill him for certain.
Rather, Allah raised him to Himself; and Allah is Almighty, Wise.

There is none of the People of the Book but will believe in him before his death, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them. (The pronouns in this ayah are read in more than one way.)

chapters.summary_md: The ayat record a plot against Isa and Allah's plan [c1]. Allah tells Isa that He is mutawaffika (left untranslated) and the One raising him to Himself [c2]. Surah An-Nisa states that they did not kill him or crucify him but it was made to appear so to them [c3], that those who differ are in doubt [c4], and that Allah raised him to Himself [c5].
chapters.body_md:
The ayat say that they plotted and Allah plotted, and Allah is the best of plotters [c1]. Allah then said to Isa that He is mutawaffika (the Arabic word, left untranslated) and the One raising him to Himself and purifying him from those who disbelieve, and that He would make those who follow him above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection; then to Him is the return and He will judge between them in what they differed [c2].

An-Nisa mentions their saying “We killed the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, the messenger of Allah”, and says they did not kill him and did not crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them [c3]. Those who differ about it are in doubt, have no knowledge except following assumption, and did not kill him for certain [c4]. Rather, Allah raised him to Himself, and Allah is Almighty, Wise [c5]. The next ayah says that none of the People of the Book will fail to believe in him before his death and that on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them [c6].
chapters.deep_md: The matter is stated in two places that have to be read together. Al Imran 3:55 gives Allah's words to Isa, with a word (mutawaffika) that has been understood by interpreters as ‘I will cause you to die’, ‘I will take you fully’, or ‘I will take you’, and with ‘raise you to Myself’ [c2]. An-Nisa 4:157 gives four negations and an affirmation: they did not kill him, did not crucify him [c3], those who differ are in doubt [c4], and Allah raised him [c5]. The words shubbiha lahum are read in more than one way [c3]. The pronouns of 4:159 [c6] are read in more than one way (‘his death’ as that of Isa or of the one from the People of the Book). This draft states the words and the main negations and does not decide among the readings; a scholar must decide how to present them.
chapters.kids_md: Some people plotted against Isa. Allah says He is the best of planners [c1]. Allah says they did not kill him, and Allah raised him to Himself [c3][c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the ayat contrast human plotting with Allah's plan [c1] and set certain knowledge against assumption [c4]. A reader may reflect on how careful a believer must be to say only what is known.
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established by the ayat: who ‘they’ are in 3:54 and 4:157, where and when the events took place, how the likeness was made to appear, who was seen to be killed, the manner of the raising, and whether Isa is alive in the heaven. The meaning of mutawaffika (3:55) and the pronouns of 4:159 are matters of disagreement among interpreters, and this draft does not resolve them. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: all accounts of a substitute, of the events of the plot, and of a return of Isa before the Day of Resurrection. Hadith to add later: the reports on the descent of Isa and on the Day, to be included only with their gradings and with scholarly review.

claims.statement_en: The likeness of Isa with Allah is as the likeness of Adam: He created him from dust, then said to him ‘Be’, and he was.

Allah tells the People of the Book not to go beyond bounds in their religion and not to say about Allah except the truth; the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, was only a messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Maryam and a spirit from Him; so believe in Allah and His messengers.

They are told not to say ‘three’; to desist, which is better for them; Allah is only one God; glory be to Him that He should have a son; to Him belongs what is in the heavens and the earth, and Allah is sufficient as a Disposer of affairs.
The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels brought near; whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant, He will gather them all to Himself.

In Surah Az-Zukhruf, when the son of Maryam was given as an example, your people turned away from it with a clamour; they said “Are our gods better, or he?”; Allah says they gave it only for argument, for they are a contentious people.
He was only a servant upon whom Allah bestowed favour, and Allah made him an example for the Children of Israel.

Allah says that if He willed He would have made angels from among them succeeding on the earth; and that he is a knowledge of the Hour, so do not doubt it and follow Me; this is a straight path; and let not Shaytan turn you away, for he is a clear enemy to you. (The pronoun of ‘he is a knowledge of the Hour’ is read in more than one way.)

When Isa came with clear proofs he said “I have come to you with wisdom, and to make clear to you some of what you differ about; so be mindful of Allah and obey me. Indeed Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is a straight path.”
The factions differed among themselves, and woe to those who wronged, from the punishment of a painful day.

chapters.summary_md: The Quran compares Isa to Adam [c1] and says he was a messenger of Allah, His word to Maryam and a spirit from Him [c2]. It says Allah is one God [c3] and that the Messiah will never disdain being a servant of Allah [c4]. Surah Az-Zukhruf adds that he was a servant given favour and made an example [c6], who told his people to worship Allah [c8].
chapters.body_md:
Allah says that the likeness of Isa with Him is as the likeness of Adam, whom He created from dust and said to ‘Be’ [c1]. He tells the People of the Book not to go beyond bounds in their religion; the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, was only a messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Maryam and a spirit from Him, so they should believe in Allah and His messengers [c2]. They should not say ‘three’; Allah is only one God, glory be to Him that He should have a son [c3]. The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels brought near [c4].

Surah Az-Zukhruf records how his example was met with clamour and the question “Are our gods better, or he?”, which Allah says was given only for argument [c5]. He was only a servant favoured by Allah and made an example for the Children of Israel [c6]. The ayat continue with Allah's statement that if He willed He would make angels succeed on the earth, and a statement about a knowledge of the Hour [c7]. Isa is quoted again saying he came with wisdom and to clarify their differences, and that Allah is his Lord and theirs [c8]. The factions differed among themselves, and woe to the wrongdoers [c9].
chapters.deep_md: Four statements about Isa's nature occur in these ayat: a creation likeness with Adam [c1], a messenger, word and spirit [c2], a servant [c4][c6], and a person who spoke to his people [c8]. The ayat that deny a son [c3] and say three [c3] address the People of the Book. The ayat that mention Isa as an example [c5][c6] are in the context of an objection to the Prophet's message. The ‘knowledge of the Hour’ clause [c7] has more than one possible referent (Isa, or the Quran) among interpreters, so this draft makes no claim from it other than the words.
chapters.kids_md: The Quran says that Isa was a servant of Allah and a messenger [c2][c6]. Allah says that Isa will never be too proud to be Allah's servant [c4]. Isa told his people to worship Allah, his Lord and their Lord [c8].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the ayat set Isa within the same pattern as other messengers: servant, messenger, and a caller to worship [c4][c6][c8]. A reader may reflect on how consistently he is described by that role.
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established: how the ‘word’ and ‘spirit’ of 4:171 are to be understood (interpreters differ), who is the ‘he’ in 43:61 (Isa or the Quran), who ‘the factions’ in 43:65 are, and the occasion of the objection in 43:57-58 (later sources give it; hadith to add later). The phrase ‘say not three’ in 4:171 does not specify what is meant by the three; this draft makes no claim about any group's belief.

claims.statement_en: Allah will say “Isa son of Maryam, did you say to the people, ‘Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah’?”

He will say “Glory be to You; it was not for me to say what I had no right to say. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my self and I do not know what is in Yours; You are the Knower of the unseen.”

He will say “I said to them only what You commanded me: ‘Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.’ I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; and when You tawaffaytani (left untranslated), You were the Watcher over them; and You are a Witness over all things.”
He will say “If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, You are the Almighty, the Wise.”

Allah will say “This is a day on which the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness; for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever; Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him; that is the great success.”
To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is in them, and He is over all things Able.

chapters.summary_md: On a Day Allah will ask Isa whether he told people to take him and his mother as gods [c1]. Isa will say glory be to Allah and that he said only what he was commanded: to worship Allah, his Lord and theirs [c2][c3]. He leaves the matter to Allah [c4]. Allah speaks of the truthful and of His dominion [c5][c6].
chapters.body_md: Allah will ask Isa son of Maryam whether he said to the people to take him and his mother as gods besides Allah [c1]. Isa will answer with glory to Allah, say that it was not for him to say what he had no right to say, and that Allah knows what is in his self while he does not know what is in Allah's [c2]. He will say that he said to them only what Allah commanded him: to worship Allah, his Lord and theirs; that he was a witness over them while he was among them, and that when Allah tawaffaytani (the Arabic word, left untranslated), Allah was the Watcher over them [c3]. He will say that if Allah punishes them they are His servants, and if He forgives them He is the Almighty, the Wise [c4]. Allah will say that it is a day on which the truthful benefit from their truthfulness, with gardens for them, and that He is pleased with them [c5]. The surah closes with the statement that the dominion of the heavens and the earth is Allah's [c6].
chapters.deep_md: This is a scene of the future, set on a day when Allah questions Isa [c1]. The answers are in four parts: praise and denial [c2], the content of what he said [c3], his limits of knowledge [c2][c3], and his entrusting of judgement [c4]. The word tawaffaytani in [c3] is the same root as mutawaffika in the chapter on the cross and the raising and is read in more than one way by interpreters. The scene is stated in the ayat as something that will be said; it is not told as a past event.
chapters.kids_md: The Quran tells of a day when Allah will ask Isa a question. Isa will say that he told people only to worship Allah, his Lord and their Lord [c3]. He will say that Allah knows everything [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the scene ends with a statement about the truthful [c5]. A reader may reflect on how it presents a prophet's account of his own words as a matter of truthfulness before Allah.
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: the time of the Day, who is listening, and the way in which the question is asked. The meaning of tawaffaytani (5:117) is read in more than one way; this draft leaves the Arabic untranslated and takes no position. Hadith to add later: reports on this Day and on the intercession.

uncertainties_en: The meaning of mutawaffika (3:55) and tawaffaytani (5:117), the words shubbiha lahum (4:157) and the pronouns of 4:159 are read in more than one way by interpreters. The draft states the words and does not choose; the chapter on the raising needs the closest scholarly review.
The identity of the Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus) and of the 'Spirit' sent to Maryam is not stated in the ayat; later tradition names Jibril. Hadith to add later.
'Sister of Harun' (19:28) is read in more than one way; the draft gives the words only.
The speaker of 19:36 and the referent of 'a knowledge of the Hour' (43:61) are not marked in the text.

Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the names of Maryam's mother, the place of the birth, the names and number of the disciples, the content of the table, and any account of a substitute or of a return. None is used in the chapters.
No dates, ages or durations appear in these chapters beyond what the ayat state; the ayat give none for the life of Isa.
Hadith to add later: reports on the descent of Isa and on the Day; each with its grading and with scholarly review.
The Gospels and other scriptures are outside this phase; the Injil is spoken of here only as the ayat speak of it.
